title.value: Cognitive Models as Simulators: The Case of Moral Decision-Making
title.justification: The title is explicitly stated at the beginning of the text provided.
title.quote: Cognitive Models as Simulators: The Case of Moral Decision-Making

extractions.description: The paper explores the use of cognitive models as simulators to reduce the training cost and time of AI systems, particularly in moral decision-making contexts. It details how AI systems, using reinforcement learning, can interact with cognitive models instead of humans to learn about fairness in the Ultimatum Game (UG). The paper also examines how training AI with these models allows the agents to adapt to emotional states, suggesting cognitive models as a potent proxy for human-like interactions in AI training.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on the application of cognitive models in AI training and moral decision-making without directly addressing climate or ecological sustainable development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Our work suggests that using cognitive models as simulators of humans is an effective approach for training AI systems, presenting an important way for computational cognitive science to make contributions to AI.

applications.value: Training reinforcement learning agents with cognitive models
applications.justification: The paper discusses using cognitive models as simulators for training AI systems in moral decision-making, specifically within the context of the Ultimatum Game.
applications.quote: Here, for the first time in the literature, we leverage this idea in the context of moral decision-making, by having RL agents learn about fairness through interacting with a cognitive model of the Ultimatum Game (UG).
